assessment.nobel_worthiness: Elucidation of GLP-1 as an incretin and its translation into long-acting agonists has changed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with documented cardiovascular and renal benefits. The physiology, the peptide chemistry and the clinical impact form a coherent discovery arc with very large patient impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1) and Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide biology and therapeutic concept) are core. Knudsen is the leading figure in the medicinal chemistry behind liraglutide and semaglutide. Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is real but its weight relative to others is contested, and the three-laureate cap forces exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs and large outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide among Mojsov, Habener-group work and others is disputed.
Whether the committee prefers to honour the physiology or the drug development is unresolved.
I have not independently verified details of the priority dispute.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells carrying chimeric antigen receptors with costimulatory domains produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. This is a new therapeutic modality, conceptually original and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB) and Sadelain (CD28 costimulation, design principles) are the clearest pair among the supplied names. Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early clinical gene-modified T cell work, but the CAR concept itself arose elsewhere (for example Eshhar, who is not among the credited names), so the credited set may not capture the whole origin.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and over a decade of follow-up; durable responses established, though toxicity management and solid tumour efficacy remain limited.
uncertainties: The original CAR concept originator is not among the credited names, which complicates a fair configuration.
Long-term safety, including secondary T-cell malignancies, is still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microbial opsins used as genetically targeted actuators allowed millisecond-precision causal control of defined neurons. This is a foundational neuroscience tool that reshaped circuit analysis, including work relevant to Parkinson's disease and depression models.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann characterised channelrhodopsin function (with Bamberg), while Deisseroth's group and Boyden demonstrated neuronal use and developed the toolkit. Six credited names against a three-person limit make this the hardest attribution on the list. Miesenböck's earlier genetically encoded photoactivation strategy adds further complexity.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for over fifteen years; clinical translation is emerging (retinal restoration) but the prize case rests on the tool and the discoveries it enabled.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth, Hegemann, Miesenböck and Nagel is unresolved.
The committee may regard a research tool as less aligned with a discovery of benefit to humankind than a therapy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib converted chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and validated rational targeting of a driver kinase, a paradigm for precision oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound programme and concept), Druker (clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio, matching prior major prize recognition. The underlying BCR-ABL discovery by Rowley, Groffen, Heisterkamp and Baltimore and others is outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of outcome data, thoroughly confirmed; recognition is late but fully mature.
uncertainties: Relation to earlier cytogenetic and oncogene discoveries not credited here, and the contribution of chemists at the company, may affect fairness.
Many committees have favoured basic mechanism over drug development; I cannot verify how that weighs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of orexin/hypocretin and the demonstration that its loss underlies narcolepsy type 1 gave a molecular explanation for a human sleep disorder and opened a pharmacological route with orexin receptor antagonists and agonists in development.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa discovered orexins and their receptors; Mignot positionally cloned the canine narcolepsy gene (hypocretin receptor 2) and showed human hypocretin deficiency. de Lecea and Kilduff independently identified the peptide, which creates a genuine priority question. A three-person selection leaves out some strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across species and clinically; suvorexant-class drugs are approved for insomnia, while agonist therapies for narcolepsy are still maturing.
uncertainties: Independent near-simultaneous discovery by the de Lecea/Kilduff group complicates credit.
Therapeutic impact so far is moderate relative to the scientific insight.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation gives robust, reversible relief of motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease and has expanded to tremor, dystonia and other indications. As a neurologist I regard it as one of the major advances in movement disorder therapy.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the single credited name and is widely recognised for introducing thalamic and subthalamic high-frequency stimulation. Other contributors (for example the subthalamic target rationale from physiological work by DeLong and others) are not among the supplied names, so a single-laureate prize could be seen as incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Tens of thousands of patients treated over three decades; the clinical evidence base is strong and the technique well established.
uncertainties: Credit relative to earlier basal ganglia circuit work and surgical pioneers outside the credited names is unresolved.
It is a symptomatic therapy with no disease modification, which may temper enthusiasm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembling L1 virus-like particles yield highly effective vaccines against HPV, now showing population-level declines in cervical precancer and cancer. This is a clear case of basic virology producing cancer prevention.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the VLP approach at the NCI, and Frazer (with Zhou) contributed early VLP production and the vaccine concept. Jian Zhou's death and the role of other groups (for example Georgetown and the University of Rochester work) leave some attribution questions; the three named people form a plausible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Real-world effectiveness data over more than fifteen years are strong, so the impact is well established.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of HPV linkage to cervical cancer (zur Hausen) may make the committee view this as follow-on work.
Competing priority claims over VLP-based vaccines have not been resolved by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstration that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that its blockade controls rheumatoid arthritis established anti-cytokine therapy and a drug class that treats many inflammatory diseases.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the translational programme from mechanistic rationale to clinical proof of concept. Other contributors to TNF biology and antibody engineering are not credited here, but the pair is a coherent configuration.
assessment.maturity: Decades of clinical use and biosimilars; very mature and well confirmed, although its recognition is not new.
uncertainties: The discovery and cloning of TNF and early antibody work lie outside the credited set.
Competition from other, potentially more novel candidates in this field and others may lower its priority.
